content:
Erin: Heads up — dedicated rollout to prod-pool-3 paused. P99 token latency jumped ~2.3x right after r3456 merge, customers on reserved capacity seeing timeouts.

deploy-bot: rollout to prod-pool-3 automatically PAUSED due to p99 > SLA threshold (2x baseline) — action required.

ci-bot: perf/regressionsuite failed on commit r3456. Test: perf/inference/p99_smoke — p99=1.92s (baseline 0.82s). Full logs: https://ci.internal/reports/1784123456/perf-fail

Dave: Ack. Is this the kernel-selection change or batching heuristic? We saw a kernel-selector tweak landed in that PR.

Carla: I started a quick bisect across merges in the rollout window. Preliminary points at r3456 -> includes batching heuristics + kernel selector fallback logic.

Ben: Profiling from a repro run on a dedicated replica (short run, mixed traces):
```
Flame top:
  42% kernel_selector::choose_best_kernel
  26% runtime::kv_cache::evict_entries
  18% batcher::assemble_batch
   6% comms::net_send_async
   8% other
```
This looks like choose_best_kernel and kv eviction spiking at the same time.

Alice: Adding kernel selection logs from the same run — we see repeated fallbacks for quantized-llama variants when seq_len > 512: 
```
2026-03-10T12:04:05Z INFO kernel_selector: attempted optimized_avx_conv for model quantized-llama-7b-q4 but constraints unmet
2026-03-10T12:04:05Z INFO kernel_selector: fallback -> generic_conv (latency +1.9x)
2026-03-10T12:04:05Z INFO runtime: kv_cache miss_rate spike=0.34
```
Looks like kernel selector failing to pick optimized kernels for a common seq_len, forcing slower code path.

Erin: Important note — r3456 changed batching heuristics to prefer assembling larger batches when backlog > 1 (to boost throughput). That increases assembly latency for the first request in the batch and extends KV cache TTL pressure; combined with kernel-fallbacks, this amplifies p99.

Carla: Repro instructions I used (short):
```
# repro with dedicated pool replica
./test_driver --pool prod-pool-3 --model quantized-llama-7b-q4 --seq-dist long --rps 120
```
Gives p99 ~2s within 90s.

Ben: Two mitigation options: 1) revert the batching heuristic change in r3456, 2) force kernel selector to whitelist optimized kernels for quantized-llama until we fix the selector constraints. Option 2 is lower-risk and faster.

Alice: I validated a hotfix patch that forces optimized kernel path when model == quantized-llama-7b-q4 and seq_len <= 2048 — locally p99 drops back to ~0.85s. Patch: 
```
// quick guard
if (model == "quantized-llama-7b-q4" && seq_len <= 2048) {
  kernel = optimized_avx_conv;
}
```
But this is a bandaid — the selector logic still has the underlying constraints mismatch on certain hardware.

Liz (PM): How many customers hit this? Any active support tickets? SLA exposure?

Erin: Two medium customers flagged increased tail latencies in the last hour, one is on a paid Dedicated contract with 99.9% p99 SLA. If we don't revert or mitigate quickly we risk an SLA incident.

Dave: Suggest we roll a temporary feature-flag rollback of the batching change (toggle prefer_larger_batches=false) and apply Alice's kernel whitelist as a short-term safe guard. That should remove the amplification loop while we properly fix kernel selector.

Carla: I can push the feature flag toggle to prod-pool-3 and stage the kernel whitelist hotfix as a canary patch. Command to toggle FF: `redwood-ops ff set prefer_larger_batches false --scope prod-pool-3`

Ben: Also adding a CI regression test to catch kernel selector fallbacks for common seq_len distributions (long-tail) — will open PR after hotfix.

Liz (PM): Please prioritize rollback + hotfix. Keep me posted on customer comms. If we need to offer credits, I'll coordinate.

deploy-bot: rollout action required: rollout remains PAUSED. Pending manual approve/resume.

Erin: I'm going to apply the feature-flag toggle now and request a hotfix patch. Will update in 10m with results. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Carla: Also leaving the bisect in case we need to point to the exact diff: candidate offending hunks in r3456 are batching.rs:prefers_larger_batches and kernel_selector/constraints.rs change set.

Ben: PR for the CI guard added: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/1287 — adds perf smoke for kernel fallback detection.

Erin: Update — FF toggle applied to prod-pool-3. Re-running perf smoke now.

ci-bot: perf/regressionsuite (post-ff-toggle) — p99=0.86s, pass.

Erin: Great — p99 back to baseline. Paused rollout will remain paused until kernel selector fix lands and CI guard merged.

Liz (PM): Thanks team. Please draft an incident note if customers escalate; otherwise mark as mitigation resolved once kernel fix in review.
